university:birmingham:waec_neco_statemen.verified_value: Medicine and Surgery (five-year) entry requirements: West Africa Examinations Council Senior School Certificate with a minimum of B2 in Science, English and Maths; A-levels or the IB must also be offered. Foundation programmes are not considered
university:birmingham:waec_neco_statemen.quote: West Africa Examinations Council: Senior School Certificate – Min of B2 in Science, English and Maths. A Levels or the IB must also be offered … BTEC, Access Courses and Foundation Programmes ⏎ We do not consider any of these qualifications.

university:manchester:waec_neco_statemen.page: https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/country-specific-information/nigeria/entry-requirements/, read 2026-10-05 via page-excerpts run 37264283845, sha256 c055a718392d6240
university:manchester:waec_neco_statemen.verified_value: General undergraduate statement (not Medicine-specific): applicants who have completed the WASSCE need to complete a University-recognised foundation programme before joining an undergraduate course. A high WAEC English grade (B3 or B2, depending on the course, taken within seven years) can usually be accepted for English
university:manchester:waec_neco_statemen.quote: Due to differences in the Nigerian and UK education systems, applicants who have completed the WASSCE will need to successfully complete a University-recognised foundation programme before joining an undergraduate course. … we can usually accept a high score in English in WAEC exams (if taken within the last seven years). The minimum grade requirement is B3 or B2 depending on the requirement of the course.

university:liverpool:waec_neco_statement.verified_value: General statement (not Medicine-specific): for English, West Africa Examinations Council (WAEC) English at Credit (4–6) or above is accepted for undergraduate degrees. The Nigeria page states no academic entry route for the WAEC certificate
university:liverpool:waec_neco_statement.quote: English language requirements for your country ⏎ Level Qualification Requirements ⏎ Undergraduate degrees West Africa Examinations Council (WAEC) Credit (4-6) or above. [the Senior Secondary School Certificate / Foundation Certificate wording in our earlier record is no longer on this page]

university:nottingham:waec_neco_statemen.verified_value: General undergraduate statement (not Medicine-specific): applicants with the standard year 12 examinations (SSC/WAEC) must complete a foundation course for entry to undergraduate programmes; foundation certificates from selected providers in the UK and Nigeria are accepted
university:nottingham:waec_neco_statemen.quote: If you have completed the standard year 12 examinations (SSC/WAEC) you must complete a foundation course for entry to our undergraduate programmes. We also accept foundation certificates from selected providers in the UK and Nigeria. [the WAEC grade profile in our earlier record is not on this page]

university:plymouth:waec_neco_statement:.verified_value: General undergraduate statement (not Medicine-specific): applicants from Nigeria should have a good Senior Secondary School Certificate (SSSC) or West African Senior School Certificate (WASSC) and an acceptable International Foundation Year or equivalent
university:plymouth:waec_neco_statement:.quote: To apply for a place on an undergraduate course from Nigeria, you should have obtained a good Senior Secondary School Certificate (SSSC) or a West African Senior School Certificate (WASSC) and an acceptable International Foundation Year or equivalent.

university:edinburgh:waec_neco_statement.page: https://www.ed.ac.uk/studying/international/country/africa/nigeria, read 2026-10-05 via page-excerpts run 37264283845, sha256 c0ce950b995837b4
university:edinburgh:waec_neco_statement.verified_value: General undergraduate statement (not Medicine-specific): applicants with the WAEC or NECO Senior School Certificate will usually be required to complete a foundation year; Edinburgh does not accept these for direct entry. Nigerian students are admitted with GCE A Levels, the IB or standardised tests (SAT, ACT or AP)
university:edinburgh:waec_neco_statement.quote: Students from Nigeria are admitted to the University of Edinburgh with a range of qualifications: GCE A Levels, the IB, Standardised Tests (SAT, ACT or AP) and other recognised regional systems. ⏎ Applicants with either the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) or the Nigerian Examinations Council (NECO) Senior School Certificate will usually be required to complete a foundation year. … The University of Edinburgh does not currently accept the above national qualification for direct entry to undergraduate study.

university:queens-belfast:waec_neco_stat.page: https://www.qub.ac.uk/Study/international-students/your-country/nigeria/, read 2026-10-05 via page-excerpts run 37264283845, sha256 c66c61b60dea6565
university:queens-belfast:waec_neco_stat.verified_value: General undergraduate statement (not Medicine-specific): the WAEC or NECO Senior School Certificate plus a recognised Foundation programme with good grades, the first year of a Nigerian bachelor's degree, the IB (30–36 points) or West African GCE / UK A Levels are considered for direct entry; grades vary by programme
university:queens-belfast:waec_neco_stat.quote: The following qualifications will be considered for direct entry to our undergraduate programmes: ⏎ West African Examinations Council (WAEC) or the Nigerian Examinations Council (NECO) Senior School Certificate plus successful completion of a recognised Foundation programme with good grades. ⏎ Applicants who have successfully completed the first year of a Nigerian University Bachelor Degree will be considered for admission. ⏎ Between 30 and 36 points in the International Baccalaureate Diploma (IB). … West African GCE A Levels or UK A Levels. ⏎ The grades required will vary according to your chosen programme.

university:sheffield:waec_neco_statement.verified_value: General statement (not Medicine-specific): WAEC West African Senior School Certificate (WASSCE) English at grade C or above can be accepted in place of IELTS. No Medicine-specific WASSCE rule is published on the Nigeria page
university:sheffield:waec_neco_statement.quote: The WAEC West African Senior School Certificate (WASSCE), English Grade C or above can be accepted in place of IELTS or equivalent.
